raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

For chat templates that only accept a leading system message (e.g. Qwen3.5), `/v1/messages` now keeps non-leading inline system messages in place by folding them into the neighbouring user or tool message, instead of merging them into the system prompt. This keeps the prompt prefix stable across turns. Fixes #63331.

## Claims

- With a system-first template, a system message that changes from turn to turn no longer changes the start of the prompt, so prefix caching covers the conversation up to that message. On Qwen3-0.6B with a system-first template, the second turn of a two-turn replay reuses 5,952 of 6,006 prompt tokens, up from 16.
- System messages that lead the `messages` array still merge into the system prompt, as before.
- Structured tool content (`tool_reference`) is never modified.
- No change when the template accepts non-leading system messages (`merge_inline_system=False`).

## Validation

**Before/after reproducer** (RTX 4060 8 GB, WSL2). I served `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` with `--enforce-eager --enable-prompt-tokens-details --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6`. Qwen3's own template accepts inline system messages, so to hit the bug I passed `--chat-template` with that template plus the Qwen3.5 `loop.first` guard. The startup warning confirms the system-first path is active. The replay sends two `/v1/messages` turns shaped like the issue's: system prompt, a ~6K-token user message, an inline system reminder, an assistant reply, then a user message. Turn 2 appends one exchange and changes the reminder's text.

| Code | Turn 2 prompt tokens | `cache_read_input_tokens` |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (be08fa5355) | 6,004 | 16 |
| this PR | 6,006 | 5,952 |

**Tests.** Each new test fails on `main` and passes with this change.

```text
# main
$ pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py -k FoldInlineSystem
3 failed, 1 passed        # each inline message was moved into a new leading system message
$ pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py -k messages_render_folds_inline_system
E   assert [1, 518, 2558...] == [1, 518, 2558...]
E     At index 15 diff: 3629 != 13
1 failed

# this PR
$ pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py
128 passed
$ pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render.py
46 passed
$ pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/
144 passed, 7 errors
```

- The 4th fold test (leading system messages still merge) passes on `main` too, by design.
- I added the `tool_reference` test after writing the first version of the fold. It failed until I added the guard.
- The 7 errors are all in `test_messages.py` and are local only. Its server asks for `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92` (7.36 GiB), and this machine has 6.88 GiB free. The same setup error occurs on `main`.
- These tests run in the existing "Entrypoints" Buildkite steps (`pytest entrypoints/anthropic` and `pytest entrypoints/scale_out`), which already depend on `vllm/`.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format`, `typos` and `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.11` are clean on the changed files.

I did not run an accuracy eval. The change only moves where inline system text appears in the prompt, and it only affects system-first templates.

## Details

- **Root cause:** `_detect_merge_inline_system` returns true when the template rejects non-leading system messages. `_convert_system_message` then appended every inline system message to the system prompt. Claude Code sends inline system messages whose text changes each turn, so the start of the prompt changed every turn. On the issue's Qwen3.8 setup, prefix hits stayed near 19K tokens per turn.
- **Fix:** `_convert_system_message` now merges only the system messages before the first non-system message. `_convert_messages` folds each later one into its neighbouring message:
  - into the preceding user message, or a tool message with string content, if that is the last converted message;
  - otherwise, for example right after an assistant turn, prepended to the next user or tool message, so nothing comes between an assistant `tool_use` and its result;
  - if no message follows, emitted as a final user message.
  - Text is joined with `\n\n`, or added as a separate text part when the content is a list.
- **Tradeoff:** a folded message loses its `system` role. Before, it also left its position. The startup warning now says this, and still recommends a `--chat-template` that accepts non-leading system messages.
- **Not a duplicate:** #56520 and #60555 change only the DeepSeek V4/V4.1 encoders. #47681 adds an opt-in `--inline-system-messages preserve` flag that is off by default. Draft #58772 has a wider design: a one-time probe through every renderer type. This PR is limited to the system-first merge path in `/v1/messages`.
- AI assistance was used to write this change. I reviewed every line and ran the commands above myself.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

LGTM. I think folding the reminder into the tool result is the right call. If it went in a separate user message instead, Qwen3.5's template would treat each reminder as a new query and drop the reasoning from the earlier tool-call steps.

I tested an issue-shaped two-turn replay on the other system-first templates in my HF cache (rendering only, no live server). The second turn now keeps almost all of the first turn as its prefix, so prefix caching can work there too.

+class TestFoldInlineSystemForSystemFirstTemplates:
+    """With ``merge_inline_system=True`` (system-first templates such as
+    Qwen's), non-leading system messages are folded into the neighbouring
+    user or tool message so a change in one does not alter the prompt
+    prefix (#63331).
+    """
+
+    def test_changing_inline_system_keeps_earlier_messages_identical(self):
+        def convert(reminder: str):
+            request = _make_request(
+                [
+                    {"role": "user", "content": "Hello"},
+                    {"role": "system", "content": reminder},
+                    {"role": "assistant", "content": "Hi"},
+                    {"role": "user", "content": "Next"},
+                ],
+                system="Top-level prompt.",
+            )
+            return _convert(request, merge_inline_system=True).messages
+
+        turn1 = convert("Reminder A")
+        turn2 = convert("Reminder B")
+
+        assert (
+            turn1[0] == turn2[0] == {"role": "system", "content": "Top-level prompt."}
+        )
+        assert turn1[1] == {"role": "user", "content": "Hello\n\nReminder A"}
+        assert turn2[1] == {"role": "user", "content": "Hello\n\nReminder B"}
+        assert turn1[2:] == turn2[2:]
+        assert [m["role"] for m in turn1] == ["system", "user", "assistant", "user"]
+
+    def test_inline_system_after_tool_result_appends_to_tool_message(self):
+        request = _make_request(
+            [
+                {"role": "user", "content": "Run it"},
+                {
+                    "role": "assistant",
+                    "content": [
+                        {"type": "tool_use", "id": "t1", "name": "run", "input": {}}
+                    ],
+                },
+                {
+                    "role": "user",
+                    "content": [
+                        {"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "t1", "content": "ok"}
+                    ],
+                },
+                {"role": "system", "content": "Reminder"},
+            ]
+        )
+        messages = _convert(request, merge_inline_system=True).messages
+
+        assert [m["role"] for m in messages] == ["user", "assistant", "tool"]
+        assert messages[2]["content"] == "ok\n\nReminder"
+
+    def test_inline_system_not_folded_into_tool_reference_content(self):
+        request = _make_request(
+            [
+                {"role": "user", "content": "Find a tool"},
+                {
+                    "role": "assistant",
+                    "content": [
+                        {"type": "tool_use", "id": "t1", "name": "search", "input": {}}
+                    ],
+                },
+                {
+                    "role": "user",
+                    "content": [
+                        {
+                            "type": "tool_result",
+                            "tool_use_id": "t1",
+                            "content": [{"type": "tool_reference", "tool_name": "run"}],
+                        }
+                    ],
+                },
+                {"role": "system", "content": "Reminder"},
+                {"role": "user", "content": "Go on"},
+            ]
+        )
+        messages = _convert(request, merge_inline_system=True).messages
+
+        assert messages[-2]["content"] == [{"type": "tool_reference", "name": "run"}]
+        assert messages[-1] == {"role": "user", "content": "Reminder\n\nGo on"}
+
+    def test_inline_system_after_assistant_prepends_to_next_user(self):
+        request = _make_request(
+            [
+                {"role": "user", "content": "Hello"},
+                {"role": "assistant", "content": "Hi"},
+                {"role": "system", "content": "Be brief."},
+                {"role": "user", "content": "What is 2 + 2?"},
+            ]
+        )
+        messages = _convert(request, merge_inline_system=True).messages
+
+        assert [m["role"] for m in messages] == ["user", "assistant", "user"]
+        assert messages[2]["content"] == "Be brief.\n\nWhat is 2 + 2?"
+
+    def test_trailing_inline_system_after_assistant_becomes_user_message(self):
+        request = _make_request(
+            [
+                {"role": "user", "content": "Hello"},
+                {"role": "assistant", "content": "Hi"},
+                {"role": "system", "content": "One."},
+                {"role": "system", "content": "Two."},
+            ]
+        )
+        messages = _convert(request, merge_inline_system=True).messages
+
+        assert messages[-2:] == [
+            {"role": "assistant", "content": "Hi"},
+            {"role": "user", "content": "One.\n\nTwo."},
+        ]
+
+    def test_leading_inline_system_still_merges_into_system_prompt(self):
+        request = _make_request(
+            [
+                {"role": "system", "content": " Leading."},
+                {"role": "user", "content": "Hello"},
+            ],
+            system="Top-level prompt.",
+        )
+        messages = _convert(request, merge_inline_system=True).messages
+
+        assert messages == [
+            {"role": "system", "content": "Top-level prompt. Leading."},
+            {"role": "user", "content": "Hello"},
+        ]
+
+
